label: <DEL> step or y input, in sequences starting with a/p/k/r/f/o/u/d
predicate: ((phase == 1) | ((phase == 0) & (in_tok == tok("y")))) & isin(orig(0), [tok("a"), tok("p"), tok("k"), tok("r"), tok("f"), tok("o"), tok("u"), tok("d")])
explanation: Fires only at the <DEL> step (56% of mass) and on original-phase inputs (44%), never in the copy phase. In the original phase it is mostly late (t>=4), first-occurrence tokens, dominated by input y (27% of mass; the strongest activations are on y) and to a lesser degree 0. Whether it fires depends on the sequence content: it is much more likely when the first original token (the upcoming first output) is a, p, or k (also r, f, o, u, d), and the second token also matters. (phase==1)|(y input) alone reaches 83% mass recall but only 8% precision, because <DEL> fires on just 7.6% of sequences. Adding the first-token condition gives dev F1 0.33 (P 0.24, R 0.57, mass 0.65). The remaining precision gap comes from a distributed dependence on prefix content that no simple predicate captures.
